messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated NCCL stall rate detected on inference-pool-4 (kv-cache path). Auto-paging oncall.
Alice Chen: got the page, jumping in. seeing lots of NCCL TIMEOUT logs on gpu-2/3, and a spike in GPU mem from kv-cache shards.
Ravi Patel: summary from metrics: within 5m we saw kv cache size per-GPU jump x6 for shard 1, while other shards stayed small. NCCL allreduce timeouts follow ~10s after.
Marta Gomez: hmm that sounds like uneven partitioning. any recent rollout that touched kv sharding or continuous batching? env changes? config deploys?
Alice Chen: yes — there was a canary yesterday that adjusted continuous batching heuristics and a runtime experiment for kv_shard_map that landed in the autoscaler config last night. canary was small but maybe it rolled further.
Sam Park: deploy-bot: deploy redwood/serving:release-2026.03.01 rolled to pool inference-pool-4 at 03:12 UTC (canary->50%).
Alice Chen: copying logs snippet from gpu-2:

```
[2026-03-01T03:22:41Z] KV_CACHE: shard_id=1 size=12.3GB entries=1.2M
[2026-03-01T03:22:47Z] NCCL: op=allreduce timeout=10050ms rank=2
[2026-03-01T03:22:48Z] OOM: GPU 2 allocation failed for kv_cache slice
```

Ravi Patel: looks like shard 1 got hot; continuous batching kept coalescing prefixes with long contexts into the same shard, blowing its memory. then NCCL suffers because one rank is overloaded -> timeouts.
Theo Nguyen: customer impact? any 5xxs surfaced to customers or increased latency errors?
Alice Chen: yes — affected routes: /v1/generate for model-x. Error rate up from 0.2% -> 8% for a subset of requests routed to inference-pool-4. Latency tail also spiked.
Marta Gomez: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable continuous batching at runtime (fast) 2) change kv_shard_map to round-robin mapping (requires restart of workers) 3) trigger rolling restart of pool with corrected shard config. Recommendation: disable batching first to stop further kv growth.
Alice Chen: doing hotpatch: setting env CONTINUOUS_BATCHING_ENABLED=false on pool config via redwoodctl.

```
# hotpatch
redwoodctl pools patch inference-pool-4 --set-env CONTINUOUS_BATCHING_ENABLED=false
```

Sam Park: applied at 03:28 UTC. Observing metrics...
Alice Chen: within ~90s, new kv cache growth rate halted. NCCL stalls count dropping. Error rate on /v1/generate down to ~1.4% and falling.
Ravi Patel: good. but persistent imbalance remains because some shards already have huge state. need plan to rebalance.
Marta Gomez: plan: create a shard remapping that evenly partitions keys by hash-range, then roll workers gradually. steps:
- prepare remap config kv_shard_strategy=hash_modulo and kv_shard_count=8
- stage config on canary node
- if canary good, rolling restart pool with new config and drain old KV state
This will require a restart of workers (no safe in-place migration for this runtime).
Alice Chen: can we avoid heavy customer impact during restarts? suggestion: increase routing to other pools (inference-pool-1/2) as temporary traffic-shed.
Sam Park: routemap: `trafficctl set-route /v1/generate --traffic inference-pool-1=70,inference-pool-2=30` executed at 03:46 UTC.
Theo Nguyen: notifying impacted customers now (CS template) — will patch status page with "degraded" and estimated mitigation 2-3 hours.


03:52 UTC - attempt canary roll of shard remap
Marta Gomez: canary applied to 1 node. running smoke tests.
Alice Chen: canary node shows normal kv sizes and no NCCL timeouts. pushing to 10%.
Ravi Patel: watchlist: per-gpu kv size, NCCL timeout count, per-route 5xx for the canary group.

04:20 UTC - after 30% rollout
Alice Chen: perf cliff noticed: one worker under 30% traffic shows high latency due to cold-cache thrash as remap enforced different key locations — but overall global NCCL stalls are down. tradeoff acceptable.
Marta Gomez: proceed with rolling restarts with 5 node batch size and 2m wait between batches.
Sam Park: rolling restart script:

```
for node in $(redwoodctl pool list-nodes inference-pool-4 --status ready); do
  redwoodctl node restart $node --env kv_shard_strategy=hash_modulo --env kv_shard_count=8
  sleep 120
done
```

Ravi Patel: executing restart. monitoring.

05:10 UTC
Alice Chen: restarted 18/24 nodes. NCCL stall metrics stabilized to baseline. per-route errors ~0.3%. kv shard sizes now distributed across GPUs.
Theo Nguyen: status page updated to "mitigated - partial" and customers told we'll keep them posted during full rollout.

06:05 UTC
Sam Park: final nodes restarted. pool healthy. rolling restart complete.
Marta Gomez: follow-ups:
- postmortem to analyze root cause: interplay of continuous batching heuristics + the new kv_shard_map rollout. include simulation of key distribution.
- add guardrails: preflight checks for per-shard memory skew on config rollouts, and an auto-throttle when a single shard grows >2x baseline in 5m.
- consider online remapping strategy (future work) and graceful kv state transfer between GPUs.

Alice Chen: handing off to Ravi for next shift. I’ll write initial incident timeline and hotfix notes.
Ravi Patel: acknowledged. I'll keep watch for 12h and follow up on postmortem invites. great job team :tada:

deploy-bot: redeploy pipeline: release-2026.03.01: note: rollback not used; config hotpatch + rolling restart applied.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated. root-cause suspected: uneven kv shard partition + continuous batching coalescing long prefixes -> shard blowup -> NCCL stalls. oncall handoff to Ravi Patel.
